Scenarios.Scenario: Open, search, scroll, and refresh the Extensions section in Agent Customizations
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Opening the visible section synchronously groups and sorts installed extensions, builds tree entries, renders the virtualized viewport, and lays out the tree. Search is delayed by 200 ms; extension changes rerender only while visible. The added warning and AI-feature labels are on this UI critical path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Installed non-built-in extensions (typically tens to hundreds) control grouping; only viewport-visible rows create warning hover listeners and at most seven fixed-list feature badges. Manifest feature checks inspect fixed lists of 8 AI points and 8 unsupported points, although warning detection enumerates each visible extension's contribution object.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single UI-thread render; searches are coalesced by the existing Delayer, hidden-section changes are deferred with renderPending, and WorkbenchObjectTree virtualizes extension rows.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The suggestions observable memoizes derived results until extension/configuration changes. Warning/label strings are recomputed when virtualized rows render rather than cached, but their fixed contribution vocabulary and viewport cardinality bound the added work; there is no cold boundary fetch.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the render, accessibility-label, hover-disposal, virtualization, and manifest-helper call paths are directly visible.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact installed-extension and viewport counts vary, but the added work remains local DOM/allocation and fixed-list manifest inspection; no changed filesystem, IPC, database, network, or subprocess call is reached.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff adds bounded per-visible-row DOM nodes, hover registrations with element-scoped disposal, and fixed-list manifest scans; it does not add collection-wide boundary fan-out, forced layout reads after writes, or unbounded retention.

Scenarios.Scenario: Enable or disable one extension from the Agents-window extension tree
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A click or keyboard action awaits the pre-existing extensionsWorkbenchService.setEnablement operation; after success the diff synchronously derives a small fixed-list contribution string and logs one telemetry event before announcing status and scheduling a render.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist workspace extension enablement and propagate extension enablement/lifecycle changes through the existing extension-management service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing enablement request per explicit user toggle, potentially including the selected extension's existing dependency/pack handling.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same setEnablement call was awaited for every toggle before this diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before status and rerender; this was already the dominant critical-path boundary before the PR.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Clean/mix the fixed telemetry payload and invoke configured telemetry appenders for agentsWindowExtensionEnablementChanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one event after each successful explicit toggle; none on cancellation/failure or when usage telemetry is disabled/metered.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No per-toggle telemetry event was emitted from this widget.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs synchronously after the awaited enablement and before status/rerender, but payload cardinality and AI-feature values are fixed and tiny.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected extension per interaction; contribution serialization scans eight fixed keys and emits a bounded comma-separated string.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each invocation awaits its own enablement operation; the diff adds no Promise.all, aggregate burst, queue, or new parallel boundary. Ordinary user interaction makes toggles low-frequency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is needed for the fixed-size telemetry payload. Enablement state remains owned by the existing service and the subsequent render reads authoritative state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the await ordering, telemetry service's synchronous cleaning/appender dispatch, and one-event tests are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Appender implementation and transport latency vary by product, but only one bounded event is added per deliberate interaction, so a meaningful latency/throughput regression is not supported.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The new telemetry boundary is bounded to one small event per successful user action and does not fan out with installed-extension count.

Scenarios.Scenario: Agents-window startup extension eligibility and after-restored auto-enablement telemetry
Scenarios.CriticalPath: During enablement-state calculation, automatic eligibility is evaluated only when Agents-window management and explicit auto-enable configuration are true. After restore, telemetry derives candidate/enabled maps from local installed extensions and may inspect existing models/statuses only when a candidate is newly observed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Eligible globally enabled extensions can participate in the existing extension-host startup/activation path when auto-enable is explicitly on.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one eligibility decision per installed extension during enablement evaluation; actual activation remains demand-driven by existing extension activation behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Auto-enablement already used canAutoEnableOnSessionsWindow and defaulted on in non-stable builds; the prior candidate list was a superset of the new list.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Potentially affects startup only for users who explicitly enable the setting. The PR changes the default to false and narrows candidates from AI plus language/review contributions to AI contributions only.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Emit existing experiment/candidate telemetry for eligible enabled extensions after workbench restore.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One enablement event per enabled candidate/enablement mode per window, deduplicated by loggedEnablements; usage events are also deduplicated per extension/usage kind.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The contribution and telemetry machinery already scanned candidates and logged these events; this diff only narrows candidate contribution types and updates test data.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Registered AfterRestored and therefore off startup's initial restore critical path; event work scales with effective enabled-candidate count.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Installed extension count N, narrowed to extensions with one of eight AI contribution points and no unsupported feature when auto-enable is explicitly true. Effective candidate cardinality cannot increase from the contribution-list change because the old list contained all new AI points plus additional language/review points.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous local eligibility scans; telemetry autorun is event-driven and deduplicated. No new parallel extension activation or boundary burst is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Derived observables memoize candidates/enabled maps until extension/configuration changes; logged sets suppress repeated telemetry for the window lifetime. There is no remote lookup or miss retry behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: configuration defaults, gating, candidate sets, AfterRestored registration, and deduplication are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Extension activation cost depends on a user's explicitly enabled setting and installed AI extensions, but PR causality points toward less startup work: default auto-enable is now false and eligibility is narrowed.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression; startup auto-enablement is disabled by default and the eligible contribution set is a strict subset of the prior set. There is not enough evidence of a shipped symptom to record this as a regression fix.

Scenarios.Scenario: Suggestion badge recomputation when installed extensions or configuration changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: When management is enabled and the badge/group observable is consumed, an extension-change signal filters the local installed extension collection and checks fixed AI contribution keys. Badge dismissal serializes the dismissed identifier set to profile storage only on explicit section navigation or visible changes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Store the dismissed suggestion identifiers in profile storage.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing store operation when dismissal adds identifiers; no write when the set size is unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same full dismissed set was stored on dismissal before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Triggered by existing navigation/visible-update behavior; the changed contribution classification may reduce identifiers but does not add the storage boundary or increase its frequency.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Installed extension count controls the local filter; effective suggestions are a subset selected by eight fixed AI keys, narrower than the previous contribution set.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Observable recomputation is synchronous and coalesced by dependency invalidation; storage writes remain one per changed dismissal set, without parallel fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Derived observables retain results until extension/configuration invalidation; dismissal state is persisted and unchanged writes are skipped by size comparison.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: observable dependencies, filtering, persistence guard, and before/after contribution sets are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Installed extension counts vary, but the PR removes candidate contribution categories and introduces no new boundary or hotter invalidation source.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression; candidate scanning remains linear local work and storage-call cardinality is unchanged or reduced.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 12 changed files and all diff pages. Traced rendering/layout, hover lifecycle, manifest scans, startup eligibility, suggestion recomputation, enablement persistence, extension-host implications, and telemetry serialization. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance issue was found.
